original_question: Let Lambda_n be the total branch length of the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n), where each edge length is its time duration. Prove that n^(-1) Var(Lambda_n) converges to 6/pi^2, and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for Lambda_n.
target_in_paper: Section 4.5, Open Problem 3, immediately after Proposition 6: "Prove that n^{-1} var(Lambda_n) converges to some limit sigma^2 and that the corresponding CLT holds." ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
correct_elements: It correctly identifies the object Lambda_n as the total length of CTCS(n) obtained by summing edge durations, and it correctly targets the paper's request for a linear-in-n variance asymptotic together with a CLT for Lambda_n. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's official statement is Open Problem 3 in Section 4.5, and it asks for convergence of Var(Lambda_n)/n to some limit sigma^2; it does not specify the value of that limit. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The constant 6/pi^2 belongs to Proposition 6, which states E[Lambda_n]/n -> 6/pi^2; in the paper this is a mean asymptotic, not a variance asymptotic. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the definition of CTCS(n) should include the split law q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i (m-i)) and the continuous-time rule that each extant m-leaf clade splits independently at rate h_{m-1}, where h_{m-1}=sum_{k=1}^{m-1} 1/k. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The range n >= 2 should be stated explicitly, since the model in Section 2 is introduced for n >= 2. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

Lambda_n should be defined exactly as the sum of all edge lengths of CTCS(n), with each edge length identified with its time duration. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The phrase "the corresponding CLT" should be unpacked explicitly; the natural stand-alone formulation is a sqrt(n)-scale limit theorem for (Lambda_n - E[Lambda_n]) centered by the exact mean, not by the asymptotic constant 6/pi^2 n. This makes explicit the normalization implicit in Open Problem 3. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

If nearby context is included, it should note that Proposition 6 is already proved in the paper, using Theorem 5 and formulas (19)-(20), so the research question should not re-ask that mean asymptotic as if it were still open. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
refined_question: For n >= 2, consider the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n) of Section 2: each extant clade of size m >= 2 splits independently at rate h_{m-1}:=sum_{k=1}^{m-1} 1/k, and when it splits it produces subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i (m-i)) for 1 <= i <= m-1. Let Lambda_n be the length of CTCS(n), i.e. the sum of all edge lengths, where each edge length is its time duration. Proposition 6 shows that E[Lambda_n]/n -> 6/pi^2. Prove that there exists a constant sigma^2 >= 0 such that Var(Lambda_n)/n -> sigma^2 as n -> infinity, and establish the associated central limit theorem (Lambda_n - E[Lambda_n]) / sqrt(n) => Normal(0, sigma^2). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
justification: Section 4.5 defines Lambda_n and places the variance/CLT question immediately after Proposition 6. The draft therefore points to Open Problem 3, not to a theorem asserting a specific variance constant. The appearance of 6/pi^2 in the draft comes from the neighboring mean result E[Lambda_n]/n -> 6/pi^2, derived from the occupation probabilities a(n,i), Theorem 5, and formulas (19)-(20). I kept the question narrow by rewriting it as Open Problem 3 with the model definition from Section 2 and by spelling out the standard normalization implicit in "the corresponding CLT." No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here, because the paper's statement is purely probabilistic. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
